Modifications: retain attested 3–11-tile German headwords in lexical POS
(excluding proper names), English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative
relationships with historical wordfreq spelling Zipf >=2.5. Omit media, examples,
quotations, etymology, translations, categories and other enrichment. Tiles use
NFC and uppercase, replacing ß with ẞ before case conversion. Ä, Ö, Ü and ẞ
are distinct single tiles; no transliteration. Borrowings with other diacritics,
hyphenated compounds and spaces are excluded. Canonical source case/spelling
are preserved separately, including German noun capitalization. A deterministic
first eligible headword is chosen when multiple source spellings share tiles;
all supplied entries remain available within display limits of eight entries
and eight senses each. Broad guesses include inflections and labelled regional,
historical or sensitive senses. Answers require a standalone eligible sense,
Zipf >=4.3 and explicit independent model editorial approval. Selection targets
contemporary standard German in Germany, not exhaustive regional separation.

Frequency: wordfreq 3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_de.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
SHA-256: 2115b5bb4adb671a3352555a480b9c2f5b03493e9f7e4047997361d62310017a
Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Software: MIT. Complete pinned README and MIT notice supplied.
Preserve all README source credits including OpenSubtitles and freely available
SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and coauthors. No corpus sentences are redistributed.
For case-normalized spellings, retain the maximum estimate, not a sum.
Historical mixed-region spelling frequency does not prove current German
commonness or sense frequency. No native-human review is claimed.

Sources, pins, policy and reproduction: docs/german-sources.md and
src/data/german/source.json in https://github.com/intrepion/kata-inspired-by-wordle-codex-dot
Preserve attribution, modification notices and ShareAlike terms when
redistributing adapted data. These notices impose no extra restrictions.

Frequency-only normalization: wordfreq upstream Unicode casefolds ß to ss. Both attested spellings therefore use the same spelling-frequency bin, without merging gameplay tiles or definitions. This can overestimate an individual spelling or sense; editorial review remains required. Primary implementation: https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/blob/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b/wordfreq/preprocess.py
